title: Help has a Tutorials menu organised in tracks, and a window that shows your progress
goal: Give the tutorials a home that stays readable as they grow. Help gets a Tutorials menu: Take the Tour at the top, then one submenu per track holding that track's guides, so nothing is ever a thirty item list. A Tutorials window is the hub: the tracks, the guides in each, how long each takes, and which ones you have finished. Both are built from the catalogue, so adding a guide adds its rows with nothing else edited.
notes:
Depends on the framework task. The catalogue and the progress store are its; this task is the IA on top.

The track list settled with the user: Basics, Redlining, Looks, Colours & Styles, Building UI, Components, Video. Order them so a new person reads them top to bottom in the order they would actually learn: Basics first, Video last.

Do NOT put a guide in two tracks. A guide that seems to belong in two is a sign the tracks are wrong, and the fix is to move it, not to list it twice.

Where the guides come from: seven sibling tasks, one per track. Expect tracks to be empty or thin while those land, so the window and the menu must read correctly with a track that has one guide in it, and a track with none must not show as a broken empty submenu.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for every tutorials task (asked for by the user on 2026-09-12):

The user's words: "I would like a help > tutorials > * set of guides which walks you through basics of various features. Maybe a nice getting started tutorial, maybe a 'building components' walkthrough, etc. ... And maybe a first run experience which lets you get an intro to the app, or just gogogo. Use the design clickthroughs as inspiration, where you have pointers and can point to various parts of the application. Build a nice framework for defining these walkthroughs so that we can extend it over time. I'd like the tutorials system to be well organized and not just a long list of things."

The agreed shape (settled in the intake conversation, 2026-09-12):
- TRACKS, not a flat list. Help > Tutorials holds "Take the Tour" plus one SUBMENU per track, and a Tutorials window is the hub. The tracks are: Basics, Redlining, Looks, Colours & Styles, Building UI, Components, Video.
- A guide is DATA, not code: a Codable value in PhotonzCore describing steps. Adding a guide means adding data to the catalogue, and the menu, the window and the progress list all pick it up with no UI edited. That is the whole point of the framework and the thing that makes it extensible.
- Steps POINT AT REAL UI, clickthrough-style: a callout with a pointer aimed at a named control, not a page of prose.
- Design doc: docs/design/tutorials.md is the source of truth for the framework and the track list, written by the foundation task and extended by the rest.

THE TRAP that will waste a runner's day if it is not read first: the app already has a registry of named UI targets, the playtest harness (playtestControl / playtestField / steady names, Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PanelTarget.swift). It looks like exactly the right thing to reuse and it is NOT USABLE here: it is compiled out of the shipping build (Scripts/build-app.sh defines PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST for the dev and probe variants only, see docs/design/playtest-harness.md, "Who can run it"), and PanelTarget.swift:141 onwards is the no-op stub release actually gets. Tutorials ship to users, so the anchor registry has to be its own thing that is compiled IN for release. Model it on the playtest one - especially the STEADY NAME idea at PanelTarget.swift:126-138, a name taken off the model rather than off the copy, so rewording a label cannot break a guide - but do not depend on it.

Existing surfaces a tutorial entry point must fit with rather than duplicate:
- The Welcome window (Sources/Photonz/Welcome/WelcomeController.swift), first-run permissions setup, re-reachable from the menu-bar menu as "Welcome & Permissions...". It already owns first launch.
- The empty-editor onboarding card (Sources/Photonz/EditorView.swift:590-615): open a file, capture a rectangle, paste an image, blank canvas.
- There is NO Help menu in the app today: EditorCommands.swift declares Capture, Image, Video, Layer and the standard groups, and macOS supplies the default Help menu. Help > Tutorials has to be created.

Queue-driven app work targets the NEXT release unless the task says otherwise (CLAUDE.md), and a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: A Help menu exists with a Tutorials submenu; the app has none today, so this creates it
Tutorials holds Take the Tour, then one submenu per track, then the Tutorials window; no flat list of every guide anywhere in the menus
Every row is generated from the catalogue: adding a guide to the data adds its menu row and its window entry, with no menu code touched, and a test proves it
The Tutorials window shows each track with its guides, the time each takes, and a clear finished mark; a track says how far through it you are
Progress is remembered between launches, per guide, and can be reset for one guide or all of them
A guide already finished can be run again without anything odd happening
Keyboard and VoiceOver reach everything: the menu rows, the window list, and the running guide's own buttons
The window conforms to the app's existing overlay and panel look rather than introducing a fourth kind of window, named in the audit
Audit under queue/audits/ with the menu and the window captured, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) Today only Basics is populated, so a literal seven-submenu menu would be six empty shelves; populatedTracks already prevents that and the menu must read correctly with exactly one track holding one guide. (2) The tour appears twice in the same menu (promoted at the top, and inside Basics). Kept: the top row is a shortcut, a track list that omits a guide is a lie, and the hub shows it under Basics too. (3) Dropped the special-cased 'Resume the Tour' copy: it only reads well for one title. A row that has been left part way now reads 'Take the Tour (step 3 of 6)', which is generic, says exactly what pressing it does, and works for every guide the seven track tasks will add. (4) Cut from the mock-ish shape: per-track progress bars, clickable step dots, and a per-row overflow menu on rows with nothing to forget. Reset is offered only where there is something to reset. (5) The hub must get out of the way: starting a guide from it closes it, or the window sits on top of the control the first step points at. (6) Menus carry no finished marks; the hub is where finished lives, and a menu full of ticks is noise.

Built. PhotonzCore gained TutorialMenu.swift: TutorialMenuModel (what Help holds) and TutorialHubModel (what the window shows), both read off the catalogue, with every word they say generated there so the copy rules run over it in a test. TutorialProgress gained forget/forgetAll/isEmpty. The app gained TutorialHubView + TutorialHubWindowController (the Experiments window's shape, not a fourth kind of surface), AppCoordinator.showTutorials, and a rebuilt Help group in EditorCommands. TutorialLauncher gained a weak registry of live editors so the hub, which has no focused editor of its own, can start a guide that teaches over your picture.

Second adversarial pass, on the running probe. (1) The menu row that carried where you got to went STALE: a command menu fixes its item titles when it is built, so after the guide was finished the row still read 'step 3 of 6'. Reproduced twice with Scripts/playtest/tutorial-hub-walk.json (the walk leaves the tour on step 2 and reads the menu bar back), including with the controller held in @State. Taken out rather than shipped wrong; progress now lives only in the window, which updates as you watch. (2) The More menu appearing on a row shoved every button on the track sideways, so its slot is now reserved whether or not the menu is there. (3) The walks were reading whatever the last run left behind, so 'tutorials' is now something a walk can forget in its setup block, and all three tutorial walks declare it.

Verified, not assumed. Scripts/test.sh: 5805 tests, 481 suites, green (one existing test updated: the playtest memory list grew by 'tutorials'). Scripts/playtest-all.sh tutorial: 3 walks green, including the new tutorial-hub-walk (50 steps). Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build menu: 12 walks green, which is the set that reads the menu bar. Real screen captures (Screen Recording granted) of the window in all three states are in the audit. The Help menu itself could not be photographed (opening a menu bar menu needs the Accessibility grant this terminal does not have), so the evidence for the menu is the exact tree the walk reads back. The window's buttons and its reading are checked through the accessibility tree, the same tree VoiceOver reads, asked of our own process: the walk fails if a button says nothing or if a guide in the catalogue is never said out loud, and it presses the row's own button to prove starting a guide closes the hub and starts the guide ('pressed "Again Take the Tour"; the hub is closed and the guide is running'). A full sweep was requested because EditorState now registers itself on canvas mount.
